newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenian shares fall prey to profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Slovenian shares fall prey to profit-taking.

text.p: Slovenian shares fell nearly one percent on Monday on profit-taking and market participants said the correction could continue over the short term.
"Foreign and domestic investors decided to take some profits and that pulled the whole market down," Toni Apollonio, an analyst at bank A Banka, said.
"However, growth will most probably resume next Monday when drug company Krka is listed, as its shares are expected to rise significantly and pull up shares of rival Lek," Apollonio said.
Krka, which will be listed on the over-the-counter (OTC) market, is currently being traded between 16,000 and 20,000 tolars per share in the grey market.
The 11-share SBI index fell 15.23 points to 1,558.8.
Market turnover tumbled to 352.9 million tolars from 1.2 billion. Overall six shares fell, eight rose and two remained unchanged, while nine were untraded.
"Turnover was low because prices seemed to have reached their current maximum last week and everyone is waiting for them to fall a bit," said Bogdan Pusnik, a trader at brokerage Medvesek Pusnik.
Since the beginning of the year the SBI index has risen 31.5 percent.
Bank SKB was the most active share, falling 2.98 percent to 73,250 tolars on volume of 2,413 shares for total turnover of 176.1 million tolars.
Preferred shares of Dolenjska bank led the day's decliners, falling 3.45 percent to 14,000 tolars on volume of 380 shares.
Financial consultancy Primofin was the biggest gainer, firming 15.71 percent to 15,980 tolars on volume of 38 shares.
On the OTC market petrol trader Istrabenz, which was listed today, was the most actively traded share, reaching 3,700 tolars on volume of 27,133 shares for total turnover of 94.2 million tolars.
